Solution 1 is wrong. Its answer $k/d$ exceeds $d$ whenever $k > d^2$, but the rigidity rank of an $n$-vertex graph in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is at most $dn$, so $C \le d$ is required. Solution 2 is wrong. Its answer $kd/2$ exceeds the trivial bound $C \le d$ whenever $k > 2$. Solution 3 is wrong. Its answer $2^{d-1}$ does not depend on $k$ and has no support in the argument it gives.

Two bounds hold for any graph with $m$ edges: the rank is at most $m = kn/2$ and at most $dn$. So $C \le \min(k/2, d)$, and none of the three expressions satisfies this for all $k \ge 1$ and $d \ge 2$.

CHOICE: NONE
